summary:
Read all 18 owned units s0002–s0019 in Chinese. No birth or age is stated anywhere in them. The only deaths are Hui (s0009, dated AD 333 through Jinshu 108), Qidegui (s0010, 奔死於外) and Zhao (s0014, 皝殺昭), and all three are captured. Era conversions are correct: Jianwu 317, Taining-end 325–326, Xianhe 9 = 334, each at year level with no Julian/Gregorian issue. The post-Hui sequence correctly uses a 333–334 event window. The repaired s0006 and mother attestations are correctly undated. There are two defects. claim-66 gives an exact AD 317 to repeated campaigns (累有功). hints-p004 lists discrete 333 and 334 values, but its owner has only window events. 68 of 70 items are supported.
Read all 9 owned units s0020–s0028 in Chinese. No birth or age is stated. The only deaths are Muti and Siluohou (s0021, 皆斬之), both captured. 咸和九年 converts cleanly to AD 334 (Emperor Cheng; Xianhe 326–334). Post-Hui backing in s0020 correctly uses a 333–334 event window. Later same-year fights (旬余, 二旬) stay at year precision. One defect: hints-p010 lists discrete AD 333 though Duan Liao's pre–Xianhe 9 event is only a window. 35 of 36 items are supported. No definite English omission/mistranslation requiring a supplemental artifact.
Read all 10 owned units s0029–s0038 in Chinese. No birth, death, or age is stated in them. 是歲 continues 咸和九年 and converts to AD 334 for the Cheng investiture, Xiangping campaign, and surrenders. 咸康初 for the Feng Yi–Sheyiyu raid is AD 335 at year precision. Three defects: claim-217/hints-p035 and claim-221/hints-p036 keep exact AD 335 for the ice strike on Ren that ZZTJ dates to 咸康二年 (AD 336); claim-222/hints-p037 date Guangwu’s Hutuo crossing to AD 25 though Hou Hanshu places it in Gengshi 2 (AD 24). 30 of 36 items are supported. English omissions in s0029 and s0032 are recorded in the supplemental artifact.
I reviewed units s0039-s0057 of Jinshu 109 (Murong Huang). The 咸康三年 kingship and appointments are correctly dated to AD 337 (Jin Emperor Cheng, Xiankang 3). The pre-kingship campaigns are correctly expressed as the window AD 335-337, from the 咸康初 anchor up to the dated kingship. Murong Ren's execution (claim-351) is over-precise at a point year AD 335 given the qualitative anchor and the winter ice-crossing. The active hints for Duan Liao, Duan Lan and Murong Jun omit their dated activity in the supplied context claims. No omitted births, deaths or ages were found. I did no external research, and this is not a full-chapter approval.
Part 5 dates the 咸康三年 (AD 337) enthronement acts in s0059 and the following Duan Liao campaign in s0060-s0066. The enthronement appointments (Lady Duan, Murong Jun) are correct point years, and the 337-338 campaign windows for Murong Huang, Duan Liao, Duan Lan, Song Hui and Shi Hu are supported uncertainty ranges. The Cao Cao and Sima Zhao rows are defective: s0059 only cites 魏武、晉文 as regency precedents in 337, so their imported regency spans and hints must become retrospective references. No unit in s0058-s0066 states a birth, death or age. This is not a full chapter approval.
Part 6 covers s0067-s0076 after Huang’s 咸康三年 kingship. Ke’s sortie, Fancheng garrison and Miyun ambush (with Ma Qiu, Yang Yu and Xianyu Liang) correctly use a 337-338 window: Jinshu is undated locally and ZZTJ places them in Xiankang 4 (AD 338). The s0072 Jin titles are mis-anchored to sourceDate 咸康三年 and hint AD 337; ZZTJ gives Xiankang 4/4 = AD 338. All s0073-s0076 claims that borrow 又聞庾亮薨 / AD 340 are wrong: that clause starts at s0077, Yu Liang died in Xiankang 6/1 (AD 340), and ZZTJ dates Ping’s Liaoxi victory, Duan Liao’s death and Liu Xiang’s embassy to Xiankang 5 (AD 339). claim-437 misreads 雖稱燕王 as a 340 assumption. No birth or age appears in these units; deaths of Huyan Huang, Zhang Zhi and Duan Liao are present. Not a full-chapter approval.
Part 7 covers units s0077–s0078 and s0220–s0255 of Jinshu 109: Murong Huang's maternal-kin memorial after hearing 庾亮薨, plus the letter to Yu Bing. Yu Liang's death (AD 340), Bing/Yi succession (AD 340), Emperor Cheng as memorial addressee (AD 340), the Su Jun–Zu Yue rising (AD 327–328), and Empress Dowager Yu's death (AD 328) are supported from the Chinese with Chengdi-annals conversions. The Zhou–Han exempla (Shen Bo through Zhang Yu) are defective in the same way as part 5's Cao Cao/Sima Zhao rows: they are only cited in the AD 340 memorial, yet carry imported life spans and active hints. Separately, hints-p083 merges 327–328 and 340 into one career window, and claim-573/hints-p097 assign Emperor Cheng a reign-wide 325–342 span for undated 陛下. No birth or age is stated in the owned units; the only deaths are Yu Liang and the Empress Dowager. This is not a full-chapter approval.

Part 9 covers Jinshu 109 units s0092–s0110: Murong Huang’s 咸康七年 Longcheng move and Goguryeo/Wandu war, 明年 Gao Zhao submission with return of Li’s corpse, then undated Moqian Hun, farming, Yuwen Gui/Sheyiyu, Changli/Weide, victory feast, and park-oxen shares. Jinshu’s own year-words convert as 咸康七年→AD 341 and 明年→AD 342, but ZZTJ 卷097 spreads the same arc across 咸康八年 (342 move and Wandu), 建元元年 (343 submission and Moqian Hun), 建元二年 (344 Yuwen destruction and Sheyiyu’s death), and 永和元年 (345 park levy). Every owned point year and hint that collapses that arc is incorrect. Separately, claim-825/hints-p126 import a 300–331 Micheon reign for Li that the chapter never states—Li appears only as a corpse. No birth or age is stated in the owned units; the only death is Sheyiyu’s. This is not a full-chapter approval.

Part 10 covers Jinshu 109 units s0111–s0112 and s0262–s0296: the park-oxen share rule and Feng Yu’s long remonstrance with historical exempla (漢祖, 明/章, 先王 Murong Hui, 西伯, 石季龍, 堯/湯, 西門/史起) and the Wang Xian–Liu Ming–Song Gai counsel episode. Jinshu never years this block; ZZTJ 卷097 places the levy and remonstrance in 永和元年 (AD 345). Every owned AD 342 point year/hint under synthetic 咸康七年後明年及隨後紀事 is incorrect, and Wang Xian/Liu Ming are 前者 even relative to that speech. Supported: Han Gaozu BC 202–195 as a reign uncertainty window; Ming AD 57–75 and Zhang AD 75–88 inside 明、章之際; Yao/Tang as legendary antiquity. Incorrect inventions: Hui 307–333 career window, 西伯 BC 1100–1050, Shi Hu 334–349 reign window from a taunt, Ximen point BC 400, Shi Qi BC 350–300. No birth or age is stated in the owned units; no death is narrated here. English supplement: s0273 十有四 misread as fourteen-in-ten; s0282 鄭白 treated as a person. This is not a full-chapter approval.
Not approved. Part 11 covers Jinshu 109 units s0297–s0303 and s0113–s0143: Feng Yu’s remonstrance and Huang’s reply restoring Wang Xian and Liu Ming, the Longshan dragons and schools, Murong Ke’s Nansu strike, the 三年 Puyu raid with Jun and Ke, later undated administration, and the cinnabar-robed omen before Huang’s Yonghe 4 death. Jinshu never dates the remonstrance or Nansu locally; the pack fills them with AD 334-348 from 在位十五年…永和四年, which is a reign-long activity span, while ZZTJ 卷097 places that block and 拔南蘇 in 永和元年 (AD 345). Bare 三年 for Puyu is converted to AD 336 as Huang-year 3, but narrative order beside 永和四年 favors 永和三年 (AD 347), and ZZTJ narrates the raid under 永和二年 (AD 346) after Huang 自稱十二年 in 345—so every 336 point year and matching hint is incorrect. The omen’s AD 348 link through the continuous hunt–injury–death chain is supported. No birth or age is stated in the owned units; Huang’s death year is context-only here. This is not a full-chapter approval.
Independent review of Jinshu 109 units s0144-s0181. Explicit dates hold: Huang died in Yonghe 4 (AD 348) at 52 sui, and Han's campaign, wound and death are Jianyuan 2 (AD 344), corroborated by ZZTJ 97. The defects are an invented AD 307 start for Hui's undated appointment of Han, Huang's 334-348 reign borrowed for the AD 338 Duan and Shi Hu events, Duan Liao's 338 flight misdated to 344, Jun's 352 imperial claim and posthumous title given as a window, a reign-wide Huang window, a retrospective 先王 reference treated as Hui's life, and an undated mother given a window. Duplicate identities are flagged. The job is not approved.
Independent review of the Yang Yu biography units s0182-s0219, checked against the Zizhi Tongjian. Supported: the 314 fall of Ji, the 338 fall of Lingzhi, and the 342 move to Helong. Found defective: He Yan (≤304), Wang Jun 領州 (304), Duan Jilujuan (314, died 318), the remonstrance (≤338), Yang Yu's death (341-348), and the Longcheng works (341-342). Undated facts carry invented windows, and allusions are dated by the ancients' lifespans. Events in the twelfth month of Xiankang 4 need a Gregorian check. Items: 17 supported, 39 flagged. This is not a full-chapter approval.
